title: Logo evolution — sketch, wireframe and render
slide_intent: Connect an identity’s visual form to a construction idea so the viewer can understand how the finished symbol was developed.
strategic_value: A recurring central axis can give Swisscom’s varied services a shared visual premise, as described in the accompanying case-study text.
demonstration: Three stages align horizontally on white: a dark hand-drawn study, a gray wireframe and a finished red-and-blue dimensional symbol.
practical_value: Trace the central axis and curved profiles through sketch, model and render to judge whether a finish preserves the original concept.

content_islands.name: Sketch
content_islands.spec: Place the rough dark drawing at left, retaining its visible central axis and layered exploratory strokes.

content_islands.name: Wireframe
content_islands.spec: Center the line model at comparable height to expose the structure without color or surface shading.

content_islands.name: Finished symbol
content_islands.spec: Place the colored render at right so the viewer can compare its shape with the two preceding stages.

ingredient.name: Central-axis symbol
ingredient.role: Give the identity a shared organizing form.
ingredient.application: Develop the visible curved surfaces around one axis and compare the form across sketch, wireframe and finished rendering.
ingredient.scope: This is a development sequence. The accompanying agency text describes life coming together around one axis; the image supplies no numerical construction dimensions.

reference_purposes.Intent: The accompanying “Unifying a complex brand” text explains the aim of a coherent “one Swisscom” around life coming together at one axis.
reference_purposes.Expression: The finished red-and-blue dimensional symbol appears beside its earlier construction stages.
reference_purposes.Application: The three-stage sequence shows the organizing form carried from sketch through wireframe to rendering.
